title: Gulf attacks on Saudi refineries and Kuwait lift oil to near $97; Sensex falls 989 points
dek: A projectile hit Aramco's Jazan refinery, killing a Nepali worker, after the Houthis claimed a strike on Ras Tanura; drones killed two Italians in Kuwait. India calls attacks on shipping 'unacceptable'.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Attacks on oil installations and shipping across the Gulf over three days have pushed oil prices to their first weekly rise this month, with Brent crude trading between about $96 and $98 a barrel on Friday. A projectile struck Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery on Thursday, killing a Nepali worker, a day after Yemen's Houthi movement claimed a strike on Ras Tanura, the kingdom's largest refinery and a main crude export terminal.

In Kuwait, two Italian technicians were killed on Thursday when drones hit a military site, Italy's foreign minister said, in an attack Kuwait blamed on Iran and Iran denied. The new supply fears hit Indian shares on Friday: the Sensex fell 989 points, ending a two-day rally, as oil rose. India, which imports most of its crude and has millions of citizens working in the Gulf, has condemned the attacks on Saudi Arabia, and External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar on Friday called attacks on shipping and seafarers "simply unacceptable".

## What happened

Saudi Arabia's energy ministry said a "hostile aerial projectile" hit the Jazan refinery on Thursday, killing a Nepali worker and injuring several others, according to its statement carried by the Saudi Press Agency and cited in reports. The ministry said the fire was brought under control, some operations were temporarily halted, and emergency and technical teams were assessing the damage. It did not name the attacker or say when full operations would resume. The refinery, on the Red Sea coast near the Yemeni border, is designed to process up to 400,000 barrels of crude a day.

The Saudi-led coalition fighting in Yemen blamed the Houthis and said it had destroyed a ballistic missile launch platform in Yemen's Hodeidah province that it said had been used in the attack. Reports differed on whether the Houthis had themselves claimed the Jazan strike.

On Wednesday, Mr Saree said Houthi drones had hit Ras Tanura on the Gulf coast and caused a fire, and that the strikes "were accurate and direct", according to reports. The coalition gave a different account: it said its air defences had intercepted and destroyed four drones over Ras Tanura, with debris falling but no injuries. A shipping source said oil loadings at the terminal were suspended after the attack, one report said; Saudi Arabia has not commented on loadings, and it was not clear by Friday whether they had resumed. The coalition also said a Houthi projectile hit Jazan port on Wednesday, causing minor damage.

The coalition said it struck what it called Houthi "operational capabilities" at Hodeidah port and destroyed targets in Saada and Amran provinces, and Houthi-run television reported Saudi airstrikes on the capital, Sanaa, on Thursday. Mr Saree said the Saudi air force had carried out 109 air and missile strikes across Yemen in 24 hours. None of these figures could be independently verified.

## Kuwait and the Strait of Hormuz

Italy's foreign minister, Antonio Tajani, said two Italian technicians were killed in what he called an Iranian attack on a Kuwaiti military facility at about 2 pm local time on Thursday, according to reports. Kuwait's armed forces said shrapnel from intercepted drones injured four people, one Kuwaiti, two Italians and one Pakistani, and its defence ministry described the attack as "Iranian aggression" against a "vital site", without naming it. Iran's embassy in Rome said it "categorically rejects" the allegation and offered condolences to the families.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said on Thursday: "We must step up pressure on Iran to put an end to these unacceptable attacks."

At sea, Iran's Revolutionary Guard said on Thursday that two tankers had caught fire after hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz, a claim not immediately confirmed by independent maritime agencies, according to reports. The UK Maritime Trade Operations centre, which tracks incidents at sea, has recorded 31 attacks in and around the strait in October and about 19 in November up to 18 November, and rates the threat there as "severe", reports said.

## The oil market

Brent, the international benchmark, was set for its first weekly gain in four weeks on Friday, with estimates of the rise ranging from about 4.5% to about 7% depending on the time of measurement. One report put it at $97.49 a barrel at 11.30 am UAE time (1 pm IST). Even so, Brent remained down nearly a fifth for November, after Middle Eastern exports had recovered earlier in the month, according to reports.

The OPEC+ group of oil producers meets on Sunday, 29 November, and delegates are considering keeping output quotas unchanged for January, according to reports. Analysts at the bank ANZ said Brent could rise above $100 a barrel even without a major new escalation in the region, one report said.

## Why it matters for India

India imports most of the crude it uses, and the Gulf supplies a large share of it, so sustained higher prices feed into the import bill, the rupee and fuel costs. On Friday the Sensex closed 989.33 points lower at 83,339.26 and the Nifty 50 fell 277.30 points to 25,607.20, with market reports linking the fall partly to oil.

The human stakes are also direct. Saudi Arabia is home to one of the largest Indian communities abroad. Two Indians were among 11 people injured in a Houthi drone strike on a Riyadh office tower on 24 November, and the Ministry of External Affairs said on 25 November that it strongly condemned "the continued attacks targeting civilian, economic and energy infrastructure" in Saudi Arabia. Nepalese workers have now been hurt or killed in both the Riyadh and Jazan attacks.

Speaking at the Indian Ocean Rim Association's ministerial meeting in New Delhi on Friday, Mr Jaishankar said attacks on maritime shipping and seafarers were "simply unacceptable" and that international law, especially the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea, "must be respected", according to reports.

## Background

Fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis, largely paused under a 2022 truce, resumed in July alongside the wider conflict between the United States and Iran, which backs the Houthis. Since then the Houthis have fired missiles and drones at Saudi airports, oil facilities and office buildings, and the coalition has carried out widespread airstrikes in Yemen.

The United States has kept a naval blockade of Iranian ports since mid-July. US Central Command says it redirected nearly 150 commercial vessels and disabled five merchant ships between mid-July and mid-November, and Iran's foreign ministry said this week that Tehran would use "all available means" to counter the blockade, according to reports.

## What happens next

Saudi Arabia has not said when the Jazan refinery will return to full operation or whether Ras Tanura loadings have resumed. OPEC+ decides on January output on Sunday. The coalition has promised a "firm military response" to attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure, which makes further exchanges likely in the coming days.

## Timeline

- 24 Nov: Drone hits Riyadh office tower; 11 injured, including two Indians
- 25 Nov: Houthis claim strike on Ras Tanura; coalition says four drones intercepted; MEA condemns attacks on Saudi Arabia
- 26 Nov: Projectile hits Jazan refinery, killing a Nepali worker; drones kill two Italians in Kuwait; Iran denies role
- 27 Nov: Brent heads for first weekly gain in four weeks; Sensex falls 989 points
- 29 Nov: OPEC+ meeting on January output
